text:
mira: quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a hybrid coalesce+debounce for continuous batching. main idea: switch between aggressive coalescing for high QPS tenants and a debounce short-wait path for low QPS to avoid headroom overcommit. wants feedback on interface change: expose an 'enqueue_hint' from frontends so scheduler can make admission decisions earlier.

alex: curious — how would enqueue_hint differ from current deadline_hint? are we duplicating signals? :thinking:

mira: good q. enqueue_hint = optional metadata (enum) with values {interactive, batchable, best_effort}. it's orthogonal to deadline_hint which is time-based. enqueue_hint lets us prefer coalesce vs debounce without relying solely on timestamps (which are noisy).

jordan: sounds reasonable. worried about trusting the client-supplied hint. malicious/buggy clients could mark everything interactive and starve others.

sam: we should combine enqueue_hint with a server-side credibility score. e.g., per-tenant weight updated by observed tail latency / SLA violations. if a tenant is flagged low-cred, we ignore their hints. simple moving average over 5m.

lee: implementation nit — do we add enqueue_hint to the protobuf Request wrapper or as an HTTP header? protobuf seems cleaner for internal services, header easier for external SDKs.

mira: proposal: protobuf field optional string + header override for backward compatibility. example for config:
```yaml
scheduler_policy:
  coalesce:
    window_ms: 6
    max_batch_tokens: 8192
  debounce:
    window_ms: 20
  hint_credit_weighing:
    interactive: 1.0
    batchable: 0.8
    best_effort: 0.3
  credibility_window_minutes: 5
```

alex: small UX: provide a simple SDK helper that maps use-case -> hint (e.g., chat -> interactive, autocomplete -> batchable). reduces incorrect hints from users.

jordan: what about headroom accounting? switching modes mid-queue could cause double-counting or eviction thrash. need tight invariants across admission and batch builder. maybe a short token-lease when switching modes so batches drain consistently.

mira: agreed — thinking lease token: when a request transitions from debounce->coalesce, it claims a transient headroom token for X ms to join an ongoing batch; if unused, token returns. prevents sudden reclaim.

sam: we should add observability hooks: sample path traces when enqueue_hint != observed behavior and histogram per-hint of queueing delay + tail P99. rollouts guarded by threshold gating.

ops-bot: deploy queued: canary config "hybrid-coalesce-debounce-v1" scheduled for 2028-04-05T15:00Z by mira. :rocket:

lee: final ask — can we run a short experiment: 2% traffic with hints enabled + credibility scoring, 2% control without hints. collect p50/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-token, batch-utilization. if numbers good, expand.

mira: yep will set up the experiment and post results in this thread. thanks all! :+1:
